title: Rabies vaccination drive for stray dogs launched in Coimbatore
summary: Coimbatore Corporation launched a city-wide rabies vaccination drive for stray dogs on April 17, 2025. The programme, inaugurated by the District Collector and attended by the Mayor, aims to vaccinate 110,074 stray dogs through mobile vaccination vehicles and four Animal Birth Control centres, continuing through February 2026.
content:
Updated- April 19, 2025 12:19 am IST - Coimbatore

A city-wide rabies vaccination drive for stray dogs was launched by the Coimbatore Corporation on April 17, 2025 at the Race Course. The programme was inaugurated by District Collector Pavankumar G. Giriyappanavar in the presence of Mayor K. Ranganayaki and Corporation Commissioner M. Sivaguru Prabakaran.

The drive aims to prevent the spread of rabies, a viral infection commonly affecting dogs. The Corporation has begun vaccinating stray dogs across all zones, and the initiative will continue till February 2026. A total of 1,10,074 stray dogs are expected to be vaccinated under the programme.

To implement the drive, the Corporation has deployed two mobile vaccination vehicles and four Animal Birth Control (ABC) centres. Each vehicle can vaccinate up to 200 dogs a day, giving a combined daily target of 400 vaccinations. The ABC centres are expected to vaccinate around 1,500 dogs every month. Each mobile team comprises a veterinarian, two dog catchers, a driver, and a support staff member.

The campaign covers all five Corporation zones. In the Central Zone, 11,017 dogs are expected to be vaccinated in one month. In the East and South Zones, vaccinations will be carried out over three months, covering 24,404 and 31,499 dogs respectively. In the West and North Zones, the drive will span two months, targeting 22,085 and 22,069 dogs.

Officials emphasized coordination between mobile teams and ABC centres to meet targets and to ensure humane handling during capture and vaccination. The prolonged timeline through February 2026 is intended to allow coverage across dense urban areas and outlying neighbourhoods while maintaining animal welfare standards.

The initiative is part of municipal efforts to control rabies and improve public health safety by reducing the incidence of the disease among stray dog populations. Local authorities will continue monitoring progress zone by zone and adjust deployment of teams and resources as needed to reach the projected vaccination totals.
